facts.statement: The genus Pravusuchus was first described by Stocker in 2010.
Pravusuchus lived during the Late Triassic (Norian stage) in Arizona, United States.
facts.quote: Pravusuchus is an extinct genus of leptosuchomorph parasuchid phytosaur known from the Late Triassic (Norian stage) of Arizona, United States.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Pravusuchus hortus.
facts.quote: Pravusuchus was first described and named by Michelle R. Stocker in 2010 and the type species is Pravusuchus hortus.

facts.statement: The generic name Pravusuchus combines the Latin word for 'evil' or 'wicked' and the Greek name for the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Latin, pravus, "evil" or "wicked", and Greek, souchus, for the Egyptian crocodile-headed god Sobek.

facts.statement: The specific name hortus means 'park' or 'grounds' in Latin.
facts.quote: The specific name, hortus, is the Latin word for park or grounds.

facts.statement: The species name refers to the Devil's Playground locality within Petrified Forest National Park where fossils were found.
facts.quote: The name refers to Devil's Playground, the locality in Petrified Forest National Park from which all specimens of this taxon were collected.

facts.statement: The genus is known from three specimens: a mostly complete holotype skull and two referred partial skulls with additional fragments.
facts.quote: Pravusuchus is known from the holotype AMNH FR 30646, mostly complete but partially disarticulated skull, and from the referred specimens PEFO 31218, a partial skull, and PEFO 34239, partial skull, partial mandible, and possible partial postcrania.

facts.statement: All known fossils of Pravusuchus come from the Sonsela Sandstone Bed of the Chinle Formation in Navajo County, Arizona.
facts.quote: All specimens referable to Pravusuchus were collected from the Sonsela Sandstone Bed (later referred to as Jasper / Rainbow Forest Bed) of the Norian-aged Sonsela Member, Chinle Formation from Navajo County, Arizona.

facts.statement: Pravusuchus is unique among phytosaurs because the lateral rim of its nostril is formed by the septomaxilla rather than the nasal bone.
facts.quote: Unlike all other phytosaurs, the lateral rim of its external naris (i.e. nostril) is formed by the "septomaxilla", and not by the nasal bone.

facts.statement: Pravusuchus possesses alveolar ridges visible from the side, a trait it shares with some other phytosaurs but not with Smilosuchus gregorii or Pseudopalatus.
facts.quote: In Pravusuchus, alveolar ridges visible in lateral view (from the sides), unlike the condition in S. gregorii and Pseudopalatus.

facts.statement: The snout of Pravusuchus is partially crested but lacks a premaxillary crest.
facts.quote: Its rostrum is partially crested, as in Leptosuchus crosbiensis, L. studeri and S. adamanensis, but it lacks a premaxillary crest, as also seen in Protome, Smilosuchus and L. crosbiensis.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Pravusuchus is the sister taxon to the Mystriosuchini clade.
facts.quote: The analysis placed Pravusuchus outside the clade containing species of Mystriosuchus and Pseudopalatus (now Machaeroprosopus), suggesting that it is the sister taxon of Mystriosuchini.

facts.statement: Pravusuchus is considered more evolutionarily derived than the genera Leptosuchus and Smilosuchus.
facts.quote: Furthermore, Pravusuchus was found to occupy a more derived position then Leptosuchus and even Smilosuchus.

facts.statement: Pravusuchus belongs to the parent group Leptosuchomorpha.
Pravusuchus is classified within the family Parasuchidae.
Pravusuchus lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Pravusuchus shares a subsidiary opisthotic process of the squamosal with the Mystriosuchini, a trait that may define a shared evolutionary group.
rejected.quote: In contrast to all other phytosaurs, Pravusuchus shares the presence of a subsidiary opisthotic process of the squamosal with Mystriosuchini, a possible synapomorphy.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'a subsidiary opisthotic process of the squamosal with'
